trial_court: Addl. Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Sagar, MC No.22/2011
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnized on 21.05.2009. The respondent was quarrelsome and doubtful by nature, causing mental harassment to the petitioner. The respondent left the matrimonial home abruptly, deserting the petitioner.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party alleging cruelty to prove specific instances of such conduct.
legal_principles.held: On meticulous appreciation of pleading and evidence on record it is evident that the appellant has made only vague allegations, without pointing out any specific instances of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: A party's failure to prove the grounds of cruelty and desertion will result in dismissal of the petition.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court has recorded the evidence. The appellant examined himself as PW.1 and marked Exs.P1 to P28. The respondent examined herself as RW.1. The Family Court based on the evidence inter alia held that the appellant has failed to prove the grounds of cruelty and desertion, hence dismissed the petition vide judgment dated 17.12.2016.

outcome.final_order: The petition filed by the appellant seeking dissolution of marriage was dismissed.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
